memories_or_initialization.description: Behavioral two-port synchronous RAM arrays reg [dw-1:0] mem[(1<<aw)-1:0] (rtl/pci_pci_tpram.v:413, rtl/pci_wb_tpram.v:414) are active because no vendor RAM define is set (rtl/pci_user_constants.v:117-133); used as FIFO storage in rtl/pci_pciw_pcir_fifos.v:391-447 and rtl/pci_wbw_wbr_fifos.v:366-422; no $readmem* initialization anywhere

hierarchy_attributes.description: synopsys translate_off/translate_on pragma pairs wrap `include "timescale.v"` and simulation-only checks in every module (e.g. rtl/pci_bridge32.v:113-115, rtl/pci_pci_tpram.v:101-103/437-461, rtl/pci_wb_tpram.v:101-103/438-462); comment-style directive '// synthesis parallel_case full_case' at rtl/pci_wb_master.v:646

unsupported_or_nonsynthesizable.description: initial blocks with $display/$finish inside synopsys translate_off (rtl/pci_pci_tpram.v:438-461, rtl/pci_wb_tpram.v:439-462); pervasive intra-assignment delays '#`FF_DELAY'/'#1' on nonblocking assignments are simulation-only (e.g. rtl/pci_in_reg.v:136-156, rtl/pci_master32_sm.v:248) and ignored/reported by synthesis

existing_sdc.basis: constraints/timing.sdc:1 'create_clock [get_ports wb_clk_i] -period 5' targets wb_clk_i, which is a top-level input port of pci_bridge32 (rtl/pci_bridge32.v:124,274), so the file applies to this top; it constrains only the WB clock and leaves pci_clk_i unconstrained

ports.name: wb_clk_i
ports.basis: rtl/pci_bridge32.v:124,274; WISHBONE clock, wire wb_clk = wb_clk_i (rtl/pci_bridge32.v:413)

ports.name: wb_rst_i
ports.basis: rtl/pci_bridge32.v:125,275; WISHBONE-side reset input feeding pci_rst_int.rst_i (rtl/pci_bridge32.v:715)

ports.name: wb_rst_o
ports.basis: rtl/pci_bridge32.v:126,276; reset output rst_o from pci_rst_int (rtl/pci_bridge32.v:434)

ports.name: wb_int_o
ports.basis: rtl/pci_bridge32.v:128,278; interrupt output (driven constant 0 in GUEST, rtl/pci_rst_int.v:165)

ports.name: pci_clk_i
ports.basis: rtl/pci_bridge32.v:169,319; PCI clock, wire pci_clk = pci_clk_i (rtl/pci_bridge32.v:412)

ports.name: pci_rst_i
ports.basis: rtl/pci_bridge32.v:170,320; PCI RST# input, source of internal reset in GUEST (rtl/pci_rst_int.v:126)

ports.name: pci_rst_oe_o
ports.basis: rtl/pci_bridge32.v:174,322; RST# output enable (constant, disabled in GUEST, rtl/pci_rst_int.v:129)

ports.name: pci_inta_i
ports.basis: rtl/pci_bridge32.v:172,324; INTA# input (unused in GUEST branch, rtl/pci_rst_int.v:139-167)

clocks.name: wb_clk
clocks.basis: rtl/pci_bridge32.v:124,274,413 (wire wb_clk = wb_clk_i); all WB-domain flops edge on posedge wb_clock_in (e.g. rtl/pci_wb_slave.v:329, rtl/pci_wb_master.v:626); no clock dividers/multipliers or gating in the design

clocks.name: pci_clk
clocks.basis: rtl/pci_bridge32.v:169,319,412 (wire pci_clk = pci_clk_i); PCI-domain flops edge on posedge clk_in fed by pci_clk (e.g. rtl/pci_in_reg.v:132, rtl/pci_io_mux.v:312-853); pci_target32_clk_en (rtl/pci_target32_clk_en.v:66-104) is a clock-enable, not a generated clock

resets.basis: PCI RST# input; internal reset = ~pci_rstn_in under GUEST (rtl/pci_rst_int.v:125-127); 'reset' asynchronously resets flops in both domains (rtl/pci_in_reg.v:132 'posedge reset_in or posedge clk_in' with clk_in=pci_clk; rtl/pci_wb_slave.v:329 'posedge wb_clock_in or posedge reset_in'); ACTIVE_LOW_OE set in rtl/pci_user_constants.v:137

Reset-role input wired to pci_rst_int.rst_i (rtl/pci_bridge32.v:275,715); in the default GUEST configuration rst_i is only consumed in the HOST branch (rtl/pci_rst_int.v:115-134), so no flop is reset by it; would be the async reset source in a HOST build

io_clock_associations.basis: WB slave inputs sampled on wb_clock_in in pci_wb_slave (rtl/pci_wb_slave_unit.v:487-544, rtl/pci_wb_slave.v:329+)
rtl/pci_wb_slave_unit.v:487-544; latched with d_incoming on wb_clock_in (rtl/pci_wb_slave.v:348-354)
rtl/pci_bridge32.v:774; consumed by pci_wbs_wbb3_2_wbb2 on wb_clk_i (rtl/pci_wbs_wbb3_2_wbb2.v:135-244)
rtl/pci_bridge32.v:775; consumed on wb_clk_i in pci_wbs_wbb3_2_wbb2
WB master read data registered on wb_clock_in (rtl/pci_target_unit.v:503,545; rtl/pci_wb_master.v:728)
rtl/pci_target_unit.v:442,734; wb_adr_o from addr_cnt_out clocked on wb_clock_in (rtl/pci_wb_master.v:490-505,734)
Registered on pci_clk in pci_in_reg (rtl/pci_bridge32.v:1616,1632; rtl/pci_in_reg.v:132-158) and used in master critical logic (rtl/pci_master32_sm.v:261-263,424-430)
Registered on pci_clk in pci_in_reg (rtl/pci_bridge32.v:1617,1633) and used in critical combinational paths (rtl/pci_target32_sm.v:290, rtl/pci_master32_sm.v:349-360)
Registered on pci_clk in pci_in_reg (rtl/pci_bridge32.v:1623,1639; rtl/pci_in_reg.v:155)
Registered on pci_clk in pci_in_reg (rtl/pci_bridge32.v:1624,1640; rtl/pci_in_reg.v:156)
Driven from pci_out_reg IOB flops clocked by clk_in=pci_clk (rtl/pci_io_mux.v:312-694; rtl/pci_bridge32.v:1431,653)
ad_en_out from pci_out_reg on pci_clk (rtl/pci_io_mux.v:312-694; rtl/pci_bridge32.v:631)
Constant from pci_rst_int under GUEST (rtl/pci_rst_int.v:128-132), assigned in the PCI reset logic block; no data sampling
WB-side interrupt crosses into the pci_clk domain via pci_synchronizer_flop (rtl/pci_bridge32.v:720,735; rtl/pci_rst_int.v:164; rtl/pci_conf_space.v:3416-3432); I/O-side association ambiguous
Driven constant 1'b0 in GUEST (rtl/pci_rst_int.v:165); no clocked driver
pci_intan_in is unused in the GUEST branch (rtl/pci_rst_int.v:139-167); effectively unconnected

clock_relationships.basis: Two independent primary clocks on ports pci_clk_i and wb_clk_i with no structural phase relation; CDC is handled with pci_synchronizer_flop two-flop synchronizers and grey-coded FIFO pointers (rtl/pci_pciw_pcir_fifos.v:565-623, rtl/pci_wbw_wbr_fifos.v:522-596, rtl/pci_delayed_sync.v:230-236, rtl/pci_conf_space.v:788-828)

unresolved: Configuration basis: sources default to GUEST (rtl/pci_user_constants.v:142-143, HOST commented out); port list, file closure and reset analysis assume GUEST + NO_CNF_IMAGE + PCI33 + PCI_WB_REV_B3 with PCI_BIST/PCI_CPCI_HS_IMPLEMENT/PCI_SPOCI inactive. A HOST build would change ports/paths and add rtl/pci_conf_cyc_addr_dec.v; SPOCI would add rtl/pci_spoci_ctrl.v; FPGA/Xilinx configs would add rtl/pci_ram_16x40d.v and vendor RAM macros.
wb_rst_i is functionally unconnected in the GUEST configuration (rtl/pci_rst_int.v:115-134 uses rst_i only in the HOST branch); it would become the internal reset source only in a HOST build.

Internal soft reset (icr_bit31 -> conf_soft_res_out, rtl/pci_conf_space.v:3929) affects only the pci_rst_o/wb_rst_o outputs (rtl/pci_rst_int.v:127), not the internal 'reset' net; not listed as a top-level reset.
pci_clk_i has no clock constraint in constraints/timing.sdc (only wb_clk_i is constrained).

rtl/pci_pci_tpram.v and rtl/pci_wb_tpram.v compile to the generic behavioral two-port RAM model because no vendor RAM define is active; ASIC flows expect these to be replaced by vendor memory macros (rtl/pci_user_constants.v:100-104), so a memory-macro dependency may be introduced by the implementation choice.

Several source lines contain apparent text corruption (e.g. rtl/pci_conf_space.v:238 '[31:( l-...)]', rtl/pci_wb_master.v:294 'latency[1]', rtl/pci_pciw_fifo_control.v:78 'wallow_out' merged with the next token, rtl/pci_spoci_ctrl.v:408 'clk_gen[1]_en', rtl/pci_wb_slave_unit.v:622), which appear to be transcription artifacts and may require repair before a clean compile.
